h1: The 6 Best Food Processors Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Food Processors Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six food processors under $200 from Ninja, Hamilton Beach, KitchenAid and Cuisinart, compared on bowl size, motor and use case.
summary: The Ninja Professional Plus 9-cup is our top pick for its 1000-peak-watt motor and preset programs. The Hamilton Beach 12-cup is the roomiest value buy, the 10-cup and 8-cup Hamilton Beach models fit lighter prep, the KitchenAid 7-cup suits brand loyalists, and the Cuisinart 4-cup is a small chopper.
intro: The most common mistake with a food processor is buying the biggest bowl and the highest wattage number without thinking about what you will actually chop. A big bowl wastes counter and cleanup time on a single onion, and a small bowl makes you work in batches for meal prep. Matching bowl size to your real habits matters more than any headline spec.

We reviewed food processors under the $200 line from their listings, ranking on bowl capacity, motor power and the functions each lists. A multi-bowl meat grinder style unit and a smaller KitchenAid chopper were left out so every pick here is a true processor or a clearly labeled compact option.

products.name: Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor, 1000PW, 9-Cup, BN601
products.verdict: The strongest motor and presets under the $200 cap.
products.description:
The Ninja BN601 has a 9-cup bowl, a 1000-peak-watt motor and Auto-iQ preset programs. It sits in the $100-200 range, the top of this price window.

It ranks first because the motor is the most powerful here and the presets simplify common tasks. Against the Hamilton Beach 12-cup, it holds fewer cups but offers more power.

Buy it if you have outgrown a budget machine and want real motor strength. The caveat is that it costs about double the Hamilton Beach models.
products.idealFor: Regular cooks who want a stronger motor.
products.skipIf: You only chop an occasional onion.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 12 Cup Stack & Snap Food Processor and Vegetable Chopper
products.verdict: The biggest bowl here at a mid-range price.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach has a 12-cup bowl, tool-free Stack & Snap assembly and a vegetable chopper mode, in the $50-100 range. The Stack & Snap design means no twist locks.

It ranks second because it offers the most capacity here for far less than the Ninja. The tradeoff is no listed wattage or presets.

Choose it for batch cooking on a budget. The caveat is that a 12-cup bowl takes cabinet space.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Food Processor & Vegetable Chopper, 10 Cups, Stainless Steel
products.verdict: Four functions and an easy-clean scraper in 10 cups.
products.description:
This 10-cup Hamilton Beach has slicing, shredding, mincing and puree functions, an easy-clean bowl scraper and a stainless steel blade, in the $50-100 range.

It ranks third because it holds two fewer cups than the 12-cup model but adds the bowl scraper. Against the 8-cup, it has more room.

Buy it for regular but moderate prep. The caveat is that the data lists no motor wattage.

products.name: KitchenAid 7-Cup Food Processor KFP0718
products.verdict: A full-size KitchenAid body for those moving up from a chopper.
products.description:
The KFP0718 has a 7-cup work bowl in a full-size KitchenAid body. The listing gives no price tier, so check the current price before buying.

It ranks fourth because 7 cups is smaller than the Hamilton Beach models and the data lists no wattage. You are paying partly for the KitchenAid name.

Buy it if brand matters and 7 cups is enough. The caveat is that the listing provides fewer specs than the others.
products.idealFor: Brand-loyal buyers moving up from a chopper.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 8 Cup Food Processor & Vegetable Chopper
products.description:
This 8-cup Hamilton Beach lists slicing, shredding, mincing and pureeing functions plus a vegetable chopper mode, in the $50-100 range.

It ranks fifth because the 10 and 12-cup models cost a similar amount and hold more. It does fit smaller cabinets.

Choose it if you want to save money for other kitchen gear. The caveat is limited capacity for large batches.
products.idealFor: Light home prep on a budget.

products.name: Cuisinart Small Food Processor, Auto-Reversing Smart Power Blade, 4-Cup
products.verdict: A 4-cup chopper with an auto-reversing blade.
products.description:
The Cuisinart is a 4-cup compact countertop unit with an auto-reversing SmartPower blade, in the $25-50 range, the lowest here.

It ranks last because it is a chopper at heart and has no slicing or shredding functions listed. In return it costs the least and takes little space.

Buy it for quick chopping jobs. The caveat is that it is not a workhorse for big batches.

whatMatters.detail: Capacity is measured in cups. A 4 cup bowl suits chopping, while 9 to 12 cups handles meal prep. A larger bowl takes more storage. Check the listed cups and compare them to your usual batch.
Wattage shows how well a machine handles dense foods. Peak watts can be higher than continuous watts, so read the label. Look for the number in the title or spec bullets.
Slicing, shredding, mincing and pureeing disks do different jobs. A chopper-only unit lacks them. Check which blades and disks are in the box.
Tool-free systems like Stack & Snap are quicker. Twist locks can be fiddly. Look at the listing photos and description for how it locks.
A bowl scraper and removable parts reduce effort. Many bowls are dishwasher safe on the top rack. Check the care note in the listing.

howToChoose.intro: Choose bowl size by how much you chop at once.

cards.text: A stronger motor handles dense foods and presets. The Ninja BN601 fits here.

cards.text: A larger bowl cuts the number of batches. The Hamilton Beach 12 and 10 cup models fit here.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to capacity unless they regularly work dense ingredients.

faq.q: Can I chop nuts in a food processor?
faq.a: Yes, but pulse in short bursts to avoid turning them into butter. A stronger motor like the Ninja helps.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Choosing by wattage alone. Bowl size and included disks matter just as much.

faq.q: Is the Ninja worth it over Hamilton Beach?
faq.a: If you want presets and a stronger motor, yes. Hamilton Beach is cheaper for plain prep.

faq.q: How do I assemble a food processor?
faq.a: Seat the bowl, place the blade or disk, add the lid and lock it. Stack & Snap models snap together without twisting.

faq.q: How do I clean the parts?
faq.a: Hand wash blades carefully, and check the listing for dishwasher safe parts.

faq.q: Can a food processor replace a blender?
faq.a: Not fully. Processors chop and slice well, but blenders handle liquids better.

finalTake: The Ninja Professional Plus 9-Cup is the best food processor under $200 for people who cook often. The Hamilton Beach 12-cup is the better value if capacity matters, and the 10 and 8-cup models cover lighter prep. The KitchenAid suits brand fans, and the Cuisinart 4-cup is a small chopper.
